steps.title: A peninsula
steps.body: Margaret River lies in the far south-west of Western Australia, about 270 km south of Perth, on a peninsula between the Indian Ocean to the west and the Southern Ocean to the south. It's about 110 km long and narrow. It has about 5,500 hectares of vines, only around 3% of Australia's, but around 20% of its premium wine.

steps.title: Maritime and mild
steps.body: Margaret River has a maritime, Mediterranean climate, among the most maritime in Australia. Oceans moderate temperatures: small differences between summer and winter, and between day and night. Most rain falls in winter. Summers are warm, not hot. Soils are gravelly, sandy loams over granite, draining well. Strong winds in spring can affect flowering.

steps.title: Its rise
steps.body: In 1965, Dr John Gladstones, an agricultural scientist, published research suggesting the region's climate was similar to Bordeaux's. Doctors founded the first wineries: Vasse Felix in 1967, then Moss Wood and Cullen. Leeuwin Estate, from the 1970s, made world-class Chardonnay. In a few decades it became one of Australia's top regions.

steps.prompt: Margaret River was compared to Bordeaux's climate in the 1960s.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Margaret River lies between two oceans in Western Australia
Its maritime climate is mild and stable
Research from 1965 led to its first wineries
